The test `test_assistant_get_work_external_task` checks whether the `get_work` method of the `CentralPlannerScheduler` class correctly handles tasks when called with an assistant parameter. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case.

Following the execution path, we find that in the `get_work` method, the condition for selecting a best task (lines 676-680) checks whether the task has resources available both on the current worker and in the greedy resource checking. If the task's resources are only available on the current worker, it is considered schedulable.

The test failure suggests that this logic is incorrect when `assistant=True`. In this case, the method does not consider the greedy resources available to other workers with higher priority tasks that share the same resources (lines 677-680).

Consequently, un-schedulable tasks are being selected as best tasks, leading to the error demonstrated by the test.

The logic of lines 676-680 is flawed when `assistant=True`. It should consider greedy resources available to other workers.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
